 ORDER
With the consent of the parties, matter is heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 20.12.2022 passed in MACC.No.563 of 2018 by 23rd Additional M.A.C.T., Jabalpur District- Jabalpur seeking enhancement of compensation.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to depositions of AW-6 Umakant Chourasia as well as Ex.P/24 to 32, submits that deceased used to purchase articles from Ms. Laxmi Grih Udyog and thereafter, he used to sale them and thereby, he was earning profit of 20-25%.

It is also urged that from cross-examination of AW-6 Umakant Chourasia, it is evident that there is no effective cross-examination of the witness on the facts he has deposed in his examination-in-chief.

Thus,
from evidence on record, including documents Ex.P/24 to 32, profession of deceased and income therefrom is clearly established.
Therefore, deceased's monthly income should have been determined as minimum Rs.25,000/- per month.
Hence, on above grounds, it is urged that appeal filed by appellant be allowed and compensation be suitably enhanced.
4. Learned counsel for respondents No.1 and 2 has supported the impugned award.

5. Learned counsel for the respondent No.3-Insurance Company submits that no documents have been filed on behalf of the appellant to prove that deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- and he was earning 20-25% of the amount spent in purchasing items vide bills Ex.24 to 32.

Therefore, in absence of relevant documents, it cannot be said that appellants have succeeded in proving Smt. Vinita Chauhan vs Balmukund on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180004300/

sentences.text: Therefore, appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

7. Sole issue involved in the case is whether income determined by the Tribunal is incorrect and whether at the time of accident, deceased was running a business of Bari/Papad and pickles etc. and thereby earning atleast Rs.25,000/- per month.
8.

With respect to above, learned counsel for the appellant has relied upon depositions of applicant witness Vineeta Singh Chouhan and applicant witness Umakant Chourasia and documents Ex.P/24 to 32.
9.

Perusal of deposition of applicant witness Vineeta Singh Chouhan reveals that she has not specifically mentioned place/manner of business whether there was any shop and if so, whether it has any name etc and if so, the place of the shop etc.

Applicant witness Vineeta Singh Chouhan has admitted in para-5 of her cross-examination that it is correct that she has not filed any documents pertaining to the shop/firm for proving sale of pickle/Bari etc.

Thus, there is nothing on record to establish the place of business/manner of business etc.
10.

Perusal of deposition of applicant witness Umakant Chourasiya and document filed by applicants reveal that there are no documents on record showing receipts of payments by deceased for purchasing articles vide bill No.Ex.24 to 32.
With respect to above, no accounts/ledgers have been filed on behalf of the applicant witness Umakant Chourasiya to prove the transactions with deceased.
Further, no documents have been produced pertaining to transportation of articles purchased from applicant witness Umakant Chourasia from Sagar to Jabalpur.
Ex.24 to 32 relates to the year 2017 and present accident occurred in the year 2017.
Further, Serial number of bill Ex.P/26 is 99 and it is dated 20.05.2017, whereas, Serial number of bill Ex.P/28 is 120 and it is dated 10.04.2017.
This discrepancy has not been clarified by non-applicant witness Umakant Chourasiya.

11. Therefore, in view of above, including nature of evidence available on record with respect to alleged profession/business of deceased, in this Court's opinion, from evidence on record, it is not established that at the time of accident, deceased was running a business of Bari/Papad and pickles etc. and he was thereby earning Rs.25,0000/- per month.
Therefore, findings recorded by the Tribunal in para-21 of impugned award with respect to above requires no interference by this Court.
12. Hence, appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.

(ACHAL KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE vai Smt. Vinita Chauhan vs Balmukund on 8 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180004300/
